The instant petition under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') has been filed by the Petitioner / Accused No.2, seeking anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.101 of 2025 on the file of III Town Police Station, Visakhapatnam Commissionerate,
which is registered for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
2.

entities.text: III Town Police Station, Visakhapatnam Commissionerate
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Heard Sri V.S.K.Krishna Kanth, learned counsel for the Petitioner / Accused No.2 and Sri K.Sandeep, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for State / Respondent.
Notice is served on Respondent No.2, but none represented on her behalf.
3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner would submit that the Petitioner herein is Accused No.2, who is a woman and she is an employee in the firm of Accused No.1.
Learned counsel would further submit that the Petitioner has nothing to do with the alleged transaction between the De facto complainant and Accused No.1 relating to the construction of flats.
It is submitted that the Petitioner has delivered a child in the month of October, 2025 and she is a milk sucking baby.

Learned counsel would submit that the Petitioner is ready to cooperate with the investigation and produce sureties to the satisfaction of the Court.
Hence, prayed to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner.

4. Learned Assistant Public Prosecution though opposed the petition, would submit that, since Accused No.1 was released on regular bail, Court may take appropriate decision in this petition by imposing stringent conditions against the Petitioner.
5. Considering the submissions made, the Criminal Petition is allowed granting anticipatory bail to the Petitioner / Accused No.2, on the following conditions:
(i) The Petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand only) with two sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the concerned Magistrate Court.
(ii) The Petitioner shall appear before the concerned Station House Officer twice in a month i.e., on every 2nd and 4th Sunday between 10.00 a.m., till 5.00 p.m., until further orders.
(iii) The Petitioner shall not directly or indirectly tamper with evidence nor influence, intimidate, or induce any prosecution witness.
(iv) The Petitioner shall surrender her passport, if any, before the Court concerned and shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court.

Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
________________________________________ Dr.JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA Date: 03.03.2026

Note: Issue C.C today B/o.
